summary.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12% YoY to INR1,063 crore, but Guinea bauxite exports fell to 1.21 Mt and EBITDA/ton slid to USD5.3.
summary.overview: Consolidated income from operations rose 12% YoY to INR1,063 crore and EBITDA edged up to INR138 crore from INR132 crore, while PBT fell to INR78 crore from INR81 crore. Guinea bauxite exports dropped to 1.21 Mt from 2.34 Mt in Q1 on monsoon disruption, higher ocean freight and fuel costs. Management reiterated a 15 Mt FY28 export target and a 5 Mt-plus target for the next two quarters, but the FY27 volume target has effectively been cut toward roughly 8.5 Mt. India businesses were pressured by freight, logistics, raw material and sulfuric acid costs, partly offset by pass-through pricing.

guidance_outlook: Guinea exports target above 5 Mt over the next two quarters (Q3 and Q4 FY27), with no quarter-by-quarter split given.
FY28 bauxite export guidance of 15 Mt reiterated; management said FY27 is well below the original plan, and the 15 Mt target was described as almost double the FY27 run-rate.
Near-term EBITDA per tonne may remain similar to Q2 levels; management said the company is close to the lower end of the EBITDA range, with some support possible in Q4 and FY28.

GSM new jetty expected by March 2027, lifting capacity from 6 Mt to 10 Mt per annum; Boffa port now at 8 Mt per annum. Management expects around 15 Mt utilisation of the combined 18 Mt port capacity in FY28.
Income tax as a percentage of PBT expected to rise over the next two to three quarters as past losses are used up; no specific rate given.
India capex planned at INR150-170 crore across verticals; longer-term target of about 40% of India turnover from new value-added products over about four years.

Iron ore: commercialisation timelines have slipped; a business-model update is expected by FY28, with possible ex-works volumes of 3-4 Mt at a few dollars margin per tonne, to be clarified by end of Q4.
capex_capacity: Boffa port fully operational, handling capacity raised from 5 Mt to 8 Mt per annum.
GSM new jetty under construction; capacity to rise from 6 Mt to 10 Mt per annum on completion, expected by March 2027.
India capex plan of INR150-170 crore across business verticals for new applications in oil and gas, paints and coatings, foundry and paper, plus volume improvement.
Iron ore: 300 sq km of resources in Guinea; exploration and infrastructure work in progress, with business model still being evaluated.
Six small bentonite mines in Gujarat awarded; management described them as small deposits and said minor-mineral acquisition is an ongoing process.
demand_pricing: Freight: the highest level reached was about USD43 (for a few weeks), and spot rates are now around USD36; longer-term rates are expected to be 10-15% lower. The C3 index has corrected 15-20% from recent highs, and forward rates are below spot.
Bauxite prices between Q2 and Q3 were broadly stable or slightly higher, per management.

Quota: no formal export quota has been issued by Guinea; management expects an update by end of the current quarter. A quota near 150 Mt versus current ~15-20% higher volume could add at least a couple of USD per tonne to EBITDA.
Middle East and European customers were hit over the last two quarters by elevated ocean freight; the company is shifting focus to domestic, Asian and African markets.
Alumina refinery demand remains sluggish; management said the company is close to the bottom of the cycle, though it cited buyers purchasing cautiously while freight stays high.
Shanghai Metal Market index described as a reasonable reference for bauxite pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Given the FY27 volume cut to about 8.5 Mt, can FY27 revenue and profit beat FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stated confidence in 15 Mt for FY28 and said freight may have peaked, with some impact possible as early as Q4. It said the company is closer to the lower end of the EBITDA range, but would not commit to beating FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current freight trend and what would take volume from 8 Mt to 15 Mt?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight is described as normalising, with the C3 index down 15-20% from highs and forward rates lower. Management said freight must improve for buyers to commit; everything else (mines, roads, ports) is in place.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA per tonne recover from USD5.3?
qa_highlights.answer: Near-term EBITDA may stay similar. Management said it was close to the bottom of the cycle; earlier USD9-10/t levels came when freight was a much smaller share of bauxite cost.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Guinea export quota and its impact?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal quota yet; an update is expected by quarter-end. Management said a quota would materially help EBITDA, and a return to prior levels of around USD8.90/t was described as the expectation if applied.

qa_highlights.question: Bauxite price trend versus Q1 and tax outlook versus FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Bauxite prices were broadly stable to slightly up from Q2 to Q3. Tax as a percentage of PBT is expected to rise over the next two to three quarters as past losses run off; no specific rate was given. Management did not commit to beating FY26 profit.

qa_highlights.question: Iron ore volumes, revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timelines have slipped, with a guidance update expected by FY28. Volumes could be 3-4 Mt at ex-works margins of a few dollars per tonne, with pricing lower than USD8-9/t; margin details will come at end-Q4.

risks_watch: Guinea volumes: H1 exports of 3.55 Mt versus the 15 Mt FY28 target; management has not given quarterly splits.
Freight and fuel costs remain elevated, tied to geopolitical events; EBITDA per tonne fell from USD6.3 in Q1 to USD5.3 in Q2.
Guinea export quota: no formal policy yet; a delay or a different structure would change the EBITDA outlook.
Rising income tax as a share of PBT as past losses are used up.
India margin pressure from sulfuric acid costs in the bleaching clay JV and from freight-driven logistics costs.
Iron ore timelines have slipped and remain speculative; the business model and guidance are still under evaluation.
Management did not respond to a question on internal negativity, and gave no detail on the Gujarat mine awards.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term numbers, with the Q2 slowdown attributed to monsoon, freight and fuel costs and India input-cost pressure. Confident on the medium term, with repeated reference to the 15 Mt FY28 target, port capacity and a possible freight recovery. Management was evasive on quantified EBITDA, FY27 profit versus FY26, and iron ore economics, and deferred several points to later quarters.
